name: Soumik Sarkar
title: Professor; Director, Translational AI Center; Associate Director, AI Institute for Resilient Agriculture
fitReason: Substantive deep RL and multimodal perception drive actual manipulation, with safe cyber-physical decision-making as a broader research theme.

physicalEvidence.summary: Find the Fruit (May 2025 primary preprint) deploys a PPO policy from Isaac Lab on a physical six-DOF MyBuddy280 arm with RealSense RGB-D sensing and ROS2. It manipulates foliage to expose an occluded target in 180 trials across four off-the-shelf artificial plants, rather than harvesting live fruit in a field. Learned high-level kinematic actions feed a conventional servo-position controller with current/torque limits. The physical best-case 86.7% result is one plant condition; the bushy out-of-distribution plant achieved 28.9%. Training-only privileged target masks are removed at deployment. The current SCS lab roster independently lists lead author Nitesh Subedi working on dual-arm/drone RL under Sarkar, establishing current directed-group linkage. Separate foundation-embedding navigation and crop datasets are not assumed to be additional physical deployments.

name: Pappu Kumar Yadav
title: Assistant Professor of Precision Agriculture AI Engineering; Principal Investigator, Machine Vision and Optical Sensor Laboratory
fitReason: Concrete neural perception-to-actuation work on a mobile agricultural platform; broader sensing research also supports practical agricultural autonomy.

physicalEvidence.summary: July 2025 primary preprint executes YOLO11 detection/segmentation on a Jetson Orin Nano mounted on a Farm-ng Amiga, using estimated canopy area to command microcontroller-controlled spray valves. Physical indoor trials use 15 potted hibiscus plants as weed proxies and water-sensitive paper to evaluate actual spraying. Outdoor soybean/corn trials and additional weed species remain future work. This is learned perception coupled to selective actuation; the study does not establish a learned driving policy or completed autonomous field weed management. Reported component/dataset numbers are internally inconsistent across sections, so no precise performance or platform-dimension claim is relied upon. The PI’s lab site independently lists the same see-and-spray project and paper coauthors/alumni, while the central university directory confirms the current SDSU appointment. Prior Florida work is not needed as the hardware basis.
